newsitem.title: CHINA: China zinc smelter seen facing huge trading losses.
newsitem.headline: China zinc smelter seen facing huge trading losses.

text.p: A Chinese zinc maker is facing enormous losses because it must buy metal on the open market to cover short positions sold earlier this year at upto almost $500 lower than current prices, industry sources said on Thursday.

Zhuzhou smelter had misjudged the zinc metal market, deciding late last year to sell forward contracts at $1,100 a tonne, an analyst at Antaike Information Co, which is part of the China National Nonferrous Metals Corp (CNNC), told Reuters.

Zhuzhou had oversold zinc at $1,100 and was being forced to clear its positions by buying the metal at current prices, now heading towards $1,600 a tonne, said the Beijing-based analyst, who declined to be named.
Officials at Zhuzhou could not be reached for comment.
"It was a case of bad judgment," the analyst said.
"Zhuzhou started selling zinc too early, when the price was at $1,100 (earlier this year). Then the price climbed and now they're preparing themselves for big losses," he said.
The London Metal Exchange (LME) official price for cash zinc was quoted at $1,570/$1,571 at the market's close on Wednesday.
Traders in Asia said they expected zinc, already around seven-year highs to move higher on Thursday to test resistance at $1,600 a tonne for three-month metal.
Chinese producers are said to be short of up to 250,000 tonnes of zinc, with Zhuzhou alone short 90,000 tonnes, according to a Chinese industry publication, China Metals.
Potential losses on these positions could be over $100 million at current market prices.
But the Aintaike analyst and other Chinese sources said CNNC would do its best to avoid this situation.
China Metals magazine quoted sources at Zhuzhou as saying CNNC was fully supporting the smelter financially.
Already, 40,000 tonnes of zinc has been borrowed from the central government reserve and reprocessed into zinc that was of a high enough standard to deliver to the LME, China Metals said.
Another smelter, Huludao, could also help Zhuzhou to fill the breach, the Antaike source said, because it made deliverable zinc and was not oversold.
Zhuzhou produces Torch brand and Huludao HX brand, both of which are registered on the LME, meaning they meet internationally accepted standards of quality, packaging and delivery.
Zhuzhou is producing metal at maximum capacity to try and meet its contracts, the Antaike analyst said from Beijing.
Huludao on the other hand, has virtually no LME short position, China Metals quoted a CNNC official as saying.
This meant Huludao, with a zinc capacity of 330,000 tonnes a year can sell the metal as it is produced, the analyst said.

A report in a newspaper based in the special economic zone of Shenzhen, where Huludao is listed on the local currency A share market, said the smelter had sold out its total zinc inventory as world prices of the metal had soared.

Customs figures showed China exported a total of 198,386 tonnes of unwrought zinc, including 7,159 tonnes of zinc alloy, in the January to May 1997 period, up 129.3 percent year-on-year, China Metals said.

Of the total, Zhuzhou exported 62,000 tonnes, 53 percent of its production so far this year, Huludao 52,000 tonnes or 41 percent of its production and Shaoguan 18,000 tonnes or 35 percent of its production, according to CNNC figures, China Metals said.
Most of that metal had headed to Japan before April 1, under Tokyo's General System of Preferences for imports from developing countries.
CNNC figures showed that its smelters had in the past few months shipped zinc to Singapore, where the LME has warehouses, at the rate of about 20,000 tonnes a month.
